items.title: Global stocks plunge amid AI slowdown fears after Democrats' midterm triumph
items.summary: Wall Street's Nasdaq fell 5.5%, its worst day in 19 months, and the FTSE 100 dropped 1.9% as investors questioned data-centre spending and returns on AI.
items.why: A funding scare offshore tends to reach Kenya slowly, so watch imported device, cloud and ad pricing before committing to annual contracts.
items.imageAlt: A trader at a share price board showing falling stock prices

items.title: Egyptian and Nigerian English join the Open ASR Leaderboard
items.summary: Hugging Face added Egyptian and Nigerian English accents to its open speech-recognition leaderboard through a data partnership with Liva AI, to test models on less-covered accents.
items.why: Voice ordering and phone support tools are usually scored on American accents, so African-accent benchmarks give buyers a way to check accuracy first.
items.imageAlt: Blog graphic with an octopus and hugging-face emoji beside the Egyptian and Nigerian flags

items.title: US warns of 'ongoing cyber threat' to retail and military freezers
items.summary: CISA and the FBI say hackers are changing temperatures on internet-connected refrigeration and cold-chain systems, after attacks in a dozen countries spoiled food.
items.why: If your cold room or fridge monitoring is online, changing default passwords and limiting remote access costs far less than losing a week of stock.
items.imageAlt: A commercial glass-door freezer cabinet with a printed information notice taped to the glass

items.title: Claude AI can plug directly into your bank account
items.summary: Claude can now link to bank and card accounts through Plaid on a read-only basis and explain balances and two years of transactions. Beta for US Pro, Max and Ultra users.
items.why: Read-only access still means handing a foreign AI service your business transaction history, so weigh data exposure before you connect a business account.
items.imageAlt: Anthropic screenshots of the Personal Finance beta in Claude showing spending charts and phone mockups

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
items.summary: Google's new video model makes clips up to 15 seconds, takes follow-up edits, keeps products and faces consistent, and costs 30% less. Generally available in the Gemini API.
items.why: Cheaper 15-second clips with steadier product shots cut the cost of making social ads for a shop, without a studio, crew or reshoot.
items.imageAlt: Google launch graphic titled Introducing Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with frames from generated clips

items.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models' identity
items.summary: Anthropic says its FlashProve system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from.
items.why: If buyers cannot tell which model made a photo or answer, trust shifts to whoever can prove provenance, a gap local sellers can price.
items.imageAlt: Anthropic logo on a dark background

items.title: Reddit is testing in-app search ads as traffic from Google declines
items.summary: Reddit is testing ads inside its search results, matched to what people search for, as it limits logged-out access after Google's AI Mode cut its search traffic.
items.why: Paid search is moving inside social apps, so a budget aimed only at Google may reach fewer buyers who are ready to spend.
items.imageAlt: Two phone screenshots of Reddit search results showing sponsored ads above organic posts

items.title: Apple starts giving Siri AI access to third-party apps
items.summary: Apple's iOS 27.3 developer preview lets third-party apps plug into Siri AI, so the assistant can act inside them and chain tasks into one spoken app skill.
items.why: Voice shortcuts let customers order without opening your app, so check that spoken requests reach a checkout that actually works.
items.imageAlt: A hand holding an iPhone with the Siri glow animation and app icons on screen

items.title: CrowdStrike launches AI kill switch that it says can stop internal agents that go rogue
items.summary: CrowdStrike added a kill switch to its Falcon Guardian platform that lets security teams stop a rogue internal AI agent, block relaunch and cut its network access.
items.why: If an agent replies to customers or places orders for you, decide now who can switch it off before a bad run touches your money.
items.imageAlt: CrowdStrike chief executive George Kurtz speaking into a microphone at a conference

items.title: AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges
items.summary: The five-year-old startup raised a $1.3 billion round led by Bessemer, doubling its valuation as demand for running AI models surged.
items.why: Cheaper, faster model serving is what makes AI features affordable for small shops; heavy funding there should push per-request prices down.
items.imageAlt: Abstract illustration of a data centre wall of servers

items.title: Itch.io adds a filter for games with gen AI disclosures
items.summary: Itch.io added a No AI browse filter; switching it on cut visible projects from 1.77 million to under 425,000, after rules asking creators to disclose AI use.
items.why: Buyers can now hide AI-assisted listings, so how you describe your process affects whether your digital work gets found.
items.imageAlt: Itch.io search results with the No AI tag filter selected in the sidebar

items.title: Netflix's new AI Discover tab helps you find something to watch based on your mood
items.summary: Netflix added an AI Discover tab whose first experimental feature recommends titles based on what a viewer is in the mood for.
items.why: Shoppers will soon expect the same: describing what they want in plain words instead of guessing keywords. Search boxes must handle that.
items.imageAlt: Person holding a remote control in front of a television

items.title: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute
items.summary: At a moment when Anthropic's compute margins should be improving, they are getting worse, showing how costly it remains to run frontier models.
items.why: AI subscriptions may not keep getting cheaper; budget for tools as a real monthly cost rather than assuming prices always fall.
items.imageAlt: Rows of server racks in a data centre

items.title: Google will let schools disable its AI tools, but not without sacrificing Search
items.summary: Schools that restrict AI altogether will lose access to Google Search, because AI features are now built into the search engine.
items.why: Search is no longer separate from AI, so product pages optimised for classic keywords need to stay readable for AI-summarised results.
items.imageAlt: The Google logo displayed on a screen

items.title: Trajectory raises $45M to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts
items.summary: The one-year-old startup is now valued at $300m; it sells tools that let people without machine-learning backgrounds train and tune models.
items.why: Model training is moving from research teams to domain experts. If that works, the bottleneck becomes data and judgement rather than ML engineering.
items.imageAlt: Three Trajectory co-founders standing in front of a slatted wood wall

items.title: Web host Squarespace lays off 19% of its employees
items.summary: Website builder Squarespace said it is cutting 19% of staff as part of a broader restructuring of the organisation.
items.why: If your store runs on a hosted builder, watch pricing and support changes; smaller teams often mean slower fixes and new upsells.
items.imageAlt: Squarespace logo on a plain background

items.title: 42AI comes out of stealth with $62.5M and a world model that can 'predict human behavior'
items.summary: The startup left stealth with $62.5m for a world model it says can anticipate what people will do in situations it has not seen before.
items.why: Predicting what a person will do next is what turns a chat model into automation that can act on someone's behalf, and that is a much harder bar to clear than answering questions.
items.imageAlt: Three 42AI founders sitting together on a couch in an office

items.title: Anthropic reports $17 billion in Q3 revenue, $895.4 billion in commitments
items.summary: Amended S-1 shows $33.2bn revenue for the nine months to 30 Sept, up roughly 1,200% year on year, and a $104bn net loss driven mostly by convertible-note revaluation.
items.why: The commitments figure shows AI demand is now booked years ahead, which means the bill has become a board-level cost line rather than an experiment.
items.imageAlt: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in glasses and a suit outside the White House in Washington

items.title: Police use facial recognition to scan one million faces in WA trial leading to 122 arrests
items.summary: Five months of WA police surveillance-van deployments scanned about one million faces, producing 122 arrests and nine false alerts, documents show.
items.why: Nine false alerts in a million scans is the number regulators will argue over, and that argument is now running in a real police deployment rather than a trial lab.
items.imageAlt: A Western Australia Police van with roof-mounted cameras parked on a street

items.title: AI is stealing Indigenous Australian art and churning out 'Temu slop', artist says
items.summary: Pitjantjatjara artist Sally Scales says generative AI is copying First Nations art without consent, as Australia weighs copyright changes for AI training.
items.why: Australia's copyright review is one of the first places where consent, not just fair use, could become a condition of training on other people's work.
items.imageAlt: Artist Sally Scales photographed near Uluru in a black top, red desert and blue sky behind her

items.title: Neoclouds: These firms you've never heard of are feeding fears the AI bubble could burst
items.summary: BBC looks at neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius, which lease GPU capacity to OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, as investors question their finances amid the AI stock sell-off.
items.why: GPU landlords are the credit risk sitting underneath the AI trade. If their financing tightens, so does the capacity everyone else has planned on.
items.imageAlt: Yellow fibre cables plugged into servers and GPUs inside the Nebius AI UK data centre in Chertsey

items.title: Anthropic's watermark rollout leaves a loophole on two older Claude models
items.summary: Anthropic is watermarking four more Claude models ahead of the EU AI Act deadline, but on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 changing sampling settings strips the mark.
items.why: A watermark that disappears when sampling settings change will not satisfy the EU AI Act's provenance expectations, however well it works in the default configuration.
items.imageAlt: Illustration of a magnifying glass held over faint watermarked text beside the Anthropic starburst logo

items.title: SpaceX loses bid to toss NAACP lawsuit over Memphis data center air pollution
items.summary: A federal judge refused to dismiss the NAACP's Clean Air Act suit, rejecting SpaceXAI's claim that its 27 gas turbines near Memphis were exempt from permits.
items.why: Data-centre power is turning into an environmental-permit fight, and courts are where AI build-out schedules actually slip.
items.imageAlt: Aerial view of the SpaceXAI data center and gas turbine power plant site under construction outside Memphis

items.title: I built an AI Tamagotchi before Meta could
items.summary: Sean Hollister turned a $50 Waveshare ESP32 pendant into a Muse-compatible AI pet using Claude Code, adding avatars and a Tamagotchi game before Meta ships Muse Charm.
items.why: A $50 pendant running a local assistant shows how quickly hobby hardware is absorbing a product category that shipped commercially this year.
items.imageAlt: A gold-rimmed pendant with a round touchscreen showing a pixel-art pet, battery level and on-screen buttons

items.title: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant, is shutting down
items.summary: Ollie, an SOC 2-certified AI assistant backed by Khosla Ventures, told users it is shutting down on 6 November after failing to compete with better-funded rivals.
items.why: A private AI assistant is proving hard to sell as a standalone subscription once the same capability is bundled free inside a chat product.
items.imageAlt: Ollie's promo image: the wordmark with the line 'Your personal AI assistant for everyday life' over a photo of a family

items.title: Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China with iOS 27.3
items.summary: Apple will ship Apple Intelligence in China: an iOS 27.3 beta on 4 November and a full release in December, with Alibaba's Qwen chatbot integrated but no new Siri AI.
items.why: Routing through Alibaba's Qwen is the template for how foreign AI reaches China, and it decides how much of the product a partner actually localises.
items.imageAlt: An iPhone on a wooden floor showing its home screen with weather widgets and a soft Apple Intelligence glow along the bottom edge

items.title: Zest's new AI agent finds restaurants and books reservations over text
items.summary: Zest launched an AI concierge that collects a group's tastes over text, puts restaurant options to a vote and books the table for everyone.
items.why: Booking a table for a group is the kind of errand that needs other people's consent, not just an API call, and that is the part agents still cannot do alone.
items.imageAlt: Screenshot of Zest's chat interface showing a text thread that suggests a French restaurant and returns a booking confirmation

items.title: Google's first data center satellite is online and writing poetry
items.summary: Google's Project Suncatcher prototype, carrying four TPUs and running DeepMind's Gemma 4, sent its first AI response from orbit and now faces radiation tests.
items.why: Orbit is the next test of where AI compute can live, and radiation tolerance decides whether Suncatcher becomes infrastructure or stays a demonstration.
items.imageAlt: A Planet Labs satellite with folded solar panels on a mount in a clean room before launch

items.title: DoorDash said it's only received 'several hundred' orders from AI agents
items.summary: DoorDash said AI agents have placed only several hundred orders so far, and that it is open to working with third-party agent makers on integration.
items.why: Agentic commerce is still a rounding error in real order volume. The integration terms being negotiated now decide whether it stays that way.
items.imageAlt: DoorDash app on a phone
